name: Bard Necrodancer
body:
Dirge bards are known for invoking the dead to empower their performances, but a necrodancer takes it a step further and calls together spirits to aid them in their performances. Necrodancers do not need to be dirge bards, but the two work very well together.

Spiritual Accompaniment (Su)

At 1st level, the bard can call up a group of spirits as a standard action to aid in their performance. The spirits can only be called when the necrodancer has their performance active.

The spirits always provide the other performance type to increase which performances may be made. For example, if the necrodancer is playing a lute and providing an auditory component, the spirits dance and caper providing a visual component. Additionally, when the necrodancer ceases maintaining their performance, the spirits maintain the benefits for 1 additional round per 4 class levels of the necrodancer. This benefit does not stack with Lingering Performance.

These spirits cannot be called up in an area affected by consecrate or any other area that prevents undead from being created. Additionally, if the spirits, or the necrodancer are affected by a spell that deals positive energy damage or destroys undead, the spirits are destroyed, but can be summoned again after 1d6 rounds.

This ability replaces bardic knowledge.
